title: HC Mike LaFleur Arizona Cardinals Press Conference 11.01.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: All right. Um, obviously, uh, a lot of injuries. Um, Jay Love had an ankle obviously didn't return. Bam Knight head neck didn't return. Kendrick Bourne ankle did not return. Um, Jaden Williams knee did not return. Reggie Virgil low back obviously didn't return. Um, so >> any particularly worrisome right now? >> What's that? >> Are any of those seeming particularly worrisome based on your initial? >> Um, I'll know more tomorrow. Uh KBs certainly didn't look good. >> Um Love was never ruled out. Was there ever a chance he could return? >> Uh not to my knowledge. So >> obviously Mike, that's a emotional kind of day with all the injuries and and you feeling the need to make a switch at quarterback and then getting the win. Just kind of where is this team right now that has to be exhilarating the way that ended up? >> I don't know if there's any words that I can express about this team right now other than they're resilient and they just keep fighting. they're always in the fight. Um, you know, um, that was a total total team effort right there. Obviously, we didn't do enough on offense and that was a collective. That was not just on one person. That was collective. Um, you know, in the first half there and and our defense kept us around. They kept us around and held a really good offense. That's a very good offense. And they and they played extremely well. I mean, shoot, they averaged 3.6 yards per play um, you know, today. And for the special teams to do what they did, miss the extra point and then come back and be resilient. I I just it's just resilient and and I'm proud of those guys. >> What went into your decision to sit Jacobe and play Mitch? I [snorts] >> I just I thought we needed a spark and again it had it was a collective deal. You know, I I need to be better with with our scheme. Obviously, I need to be better with our play calling. Um you know, and and and all of us need it. We we got a we got a lot to fix right now. And I get and and I don't want this last 30 minutes or 35 minutes to mask, you know, the stuff that we need to fix on offense. Uh because I know we're a lot better than that. I know we can execute better than that. So >> start next week. >> I I'm just excited about this win right now. So >> if that [snorts] was how it looked with those two, why not make that change earlier either today or earlier in the season? >> Yeah. I mean, again, it's uh that was that was collective. That's I know what the story is going to be and I understand that and so does he. Uh but that was collective and it starts with me. >> The offense looked better after Frier came in on on the left side when Williams went down. Why do you think that that was? >> Again I I got a lot of I got a lot of trust in Jaden Williams. I think he's going to be a dang good football player in this league and he's got the right uh you know look in his eye and he's got the right demeanor and the right approach to it. So, um, but I have a lot of, uh, trust in Frier, and I know they do, too. He he doesn't flinch either, you know. So, um, again, it was it was collective. There was there was plays that he had out in the first half. There were. And there was plays that I can call better. And we got to figure out how to execute it for 60 straight minutes, not, you know, just turn it on for basically, you know, I guess that last 30, if you will. >> What were the things that Gardner did that unlocks the offense? >> Yeah, he did a good job. I mean, obviously, uh, um, extended a few plays, stuff like that, but I thought his I thought his timing was great. I mean, he's he's he's had a lot of success in this league, guys, and and um and he's about as resilient as they come, too. Uh, if you ask Gardenner Mchu, you know, I mean, he's ready at all times. And, um, you know, I thought the guys made some plays for him, and he was getting the ball out of his hands. Obviously, you know, kind of what unlocked it to start was he starts with a six-y completion to Duivere. Uh, and then and then, you know, we obviously have that long run by TA right there. And it just kind of somewhat unlocked and loosened loosened them up. Like that's that's why you need explosives and big plays cuz it loosens people up. But I you know, again, and I'm going to flip it real quick cuz I I can't I mean the defense played played awesome. But but um ended with three receivers, one running back, and and you know, tackle going down and all those kind of things. Quarterback change, all those kind of things. And for those guys to continue to battle was was unbelievable. I've never seen anything like it from an injury standpoint in the skill position in my life. >> Seemingly handled that workload pretty well, but what what were the changes or challenges for you as a play caller with one running back? >> Yeah. Well, it nothing. It was what it was like he he couldn't come out and uh so and he knew that so he put his his his cape on and became Superman for us. And u what a cool deal too. Um you know um I'm proud of him cuz he's a resilient dude. He's exactly what you want. >> Oo line was struggling. Was part of the decision to go to Gardner to get a more mobile guy back there? >> It was again it was it was collective. >> What can you say about Michael Wilson? I mean clearly he was in pain quite often after some some plays and he finished over 100 yards, couple touchdowns or one touch. >> He's he's a stud. He's everything you want, you know, and there's a lot of these guys and we got to figure out how to, you know, put this together for 60 minutes and play, you know, the the the game that we are capable of in all three phases. But, uh, if you guys knew how how much I mean, you kind of did, but how much pain that that Mike was in and to to go out there and and do what he did and just continuing to battle and have that big run on the, you know, on the third and one. Um, proud of him. >> There was that drive in the fourth quarter where um, Collier had the unnecessary roughness and then you took sweat out cuz he was yelling at him. What went into this decision first of all to leave both of those guys in the game because then they obviously both came back with with big plays later on. Yeah, I know LJ and LJ's smarter than that. It's some guys you have to talk to in the moment. Some guys you just know and and I've already talked to LJ and um I love LJ and he knows he made a mistake right there for the team, but uh but I trust him. There's other guys and that might hopefully that never happens again that I might have to bring out there, but all you have to do is look in LJ's eyes. You you know, and um you know, obviously that can't happen, but I trust LJ. >> What [snorts] about Sweaty? >> Uh same thing. I I love Sweaty. He's he's been a stud and it's been really good to get to know him and um you know and and watch him continue to get uh better every week. >> What goes [snorts] through your head when Chad misses that extra point? >> Let's go. I mean, it is what it is. Like it's this game it I mean I don't think anyone really in this room or anyone probably in the country thought that we had a chance at coming back right there. And so to make it 3030, it was only only fitting, you know, and uh and for Chad to to finish it out for us. Um, you know, like I told the guys uh right when we started overtime, there's no way we're not coming out here with a win. Then we go three and out and uh and then our defense comes up big again and um and you know, we make enough plays on offense to get it in there and and there Chad is doing it again just like he did two weeks ago at Sofi, you know, and being resilient. Um so, uh proud of all those guys. >> You mentioned the 3.6 yards per play against a really good offense. What where did it start with the defense? that play style. Um I thought Nick had a really good game plan. I thought they had a great week. I thought uh um they're not really concerned about noise. They're just concerned about doing their job and and uh they got they got men on that defensive side. Um they're they're they're grown ass men. Um and uh they're always um excited about the opportunity to be 1 and0 every week. Um and they just kept battling today. with so many >> just the last one and then we got mission >> with so many injuries to starters being down two scores at one point. What was your message or what does it take for a team mentally to stay in and force overtime and stay in it? >> Yeah, I mean that's that's what we all signed up for. Um so it is what it is. Next man up and we just saw that at the highest level that I've ever been a part of. Um, and guy again I it got to the point where you're just like you're you're just you don't even know who you're throwing balls to at that point, you know, cuz you don't know who's mixing and matching and and and Mike's hurting and stuff like that. And so, I mean, I'm calling based on on the formation and Sime and Mike are switching themselves at the end right there. So, Simmy can do some of the griier work because of where Mike was at. And Simey's not feeling great either. Um, and it's um I just again I think you guys can tell I'm at a loss of words in terms of just how I feel for that locker room right now. And I feel for the guys that that got hurt cuz every single one of those guys um you know put their body on the line and and um you know a lot of lot of young guys in there that that I'm excited to watch you know continue to grow. We'll see what this list looks like tomorrow once we get back home and you know get some obviously a little bit more look at it. But uh yeah, proud of that locker room.

title: Atlanta Falcons players speak to the media following Tampa Bay Buccaneers matchup | Press Conference
text: Bjan, obviously really crazy rainy weather conditions, windy as well. Had you ever played in a game like this before? >> Uh, well, first off, I got to give honor to God. Um, just give him praise for getting us all healthy and just playing for him and, you know, making sure that I try to give him glory no matter win or lose. Um, but yeah, no, I haven't played a game like that before. I just played in the snow, but yeah, not a not a rain game like that. So, you know, those are game those are games that are fun that you love to play. You know, run the football, but you know, you want to win those games, too. Uh, but yeah, that was the first time. >> How did it impact the game and the way you guys were able to execute? >> Yeah, I mean, for us, like we knew what kind of game it was going to be um as soon as it kept kept raining. So, we were like, we got to run it and get yards and wear the defense down. Um, and and that's what we were doing. and and you know for us like we got to continue to capitalize on opportunities um when we get them and you know it's it's all a whole offensive effort you know we have to get a hat on the half for 11 on 111 and just just run it run it um as much as we can. >> What was the Bucks defense doing so well to kind of not let you guys get into a rhythm today? Yeah, I mean, um, you know, I think it was it was just our our own mistakes, you know, the the mistakes that we created and, you know, I think just we just can't turn it turn the ball over. Um, we got to continue to, you know, limit limit mistakes and, you know, I I made mistakes that game in the game and, you know, I got to make sure that I I'm doing right on my part so I can help this team. But, you know, they're they're a really good defense. Um, but like it doesn't matter who lines up across from us. Like we have to get the job done and do it do it at a high level. >> What are the biggest challenges for an offense in a game like this with the ball's wet and you know the field is wet and muddy? >> Yeah, I mean there there's not too much of a challenge. All you got to do is just run it efficiently and and you know that can open up some some other stuff with play action pass and stuff like that. But, you know, I know that these games are uh are wet ball games, but for us, like we can't it can't matter for us. We just got to do what we got to do to win. >> What was Coach Debansky's message after the game? >> Yeah, I mean, we we, you know, lost, you know, fair and square and we got to, you know, think about it while we're going back home and then we got to eliminate it real quick cuz we have an opponent next week. So, you know, he's making sure that we're, you know, we want to feel it and and and feel the hurt a little bit cuz, you know, I feel like that's how you become a better player. And then, you know, when we get when we get off that plane, like it's on to to Cincinnati and Madrid. >> He harps a lot about how you play the run and how you run it is who you are as a team. I think they ran it for around 3.5 and you guys ran I think 99 yards. Just to hear the margin that wide, what comes to mind? >> Yeah, I mean that sucks. That's all it is, man. like you know we do pride ourselves running the football and you know they they they did a good job on their side. Um >> but you know now it's just us to go back to the drawing board and like we always say like our identity and you know it's it takes all 11 of us to you know when you run the ball successfully it it it takes it takes a pain on the defense. Um it helps your whole team. So you know for us like now it's our job to figure out how we can get back on on track with it. um and and make sure that we're doing all the right things to to help this team win um and all in in the run game. >> How bad was >> Got two more here, y'all. >> Okay. Thanks. How um how bad were the conditions and did you all have to switch the long did y'all go to the long spikes at any point? >> Yeah. >> To start with for that matter. >> Yeah, conditions were were bad. Um you know, that's what we were dealt and you know, I think we all wore the spikes uh the whole game. I know I wear the spikes from the beginning of the game, but >> you know, when you play on on wet fields like that, like it's it's smart to to wear the seven studs just so you don't start slipping and stuff out there. But, you know, I look at it as an advantage. Um, >> you know, when the defense starts open pursuit and stuff like that, you can you can find your angles. But >> yeah, it was it was pretty bad conditions out there. >> You took your gloves off at one point, right? >> Yeah. Yeah, I did. >> Because it was >> Yeah, Mike threw me a ball. Mike threw me a ball and and the ball slipped right through. So, I was like, I gota I got to take the gloves off. Um, just go just go natural. >> We kind of knew about it coming into the game. Um, we knew what type of game it was going to be. It's probably the craziest game I've ever been a part of um in the first half. Um, but hey, anywhere, any place, any time, any type of weather, got to be ready to play. >> The wind swirling down there. I mean, we saw the rain, but we looked a little bit more than just a >> Yeah, it was it was a little bit of everything. It's just Florida for you. This felt a little bit like weeks one and two when you got behind the turnover margin early and it was a tough day defensively. Did you feel like y'all held on for a while? >> Yeah, I thought, you know, it was a n game I think up until the third quarter. >> Um, so I never thought we were going to be out of it even, uh, I think it was maybe four minutes left. I think we just had a big play with Jan. Um, still a two- possession game. U with the playmakers that we have in this in this locker room. I really thought we were going to, you know, at least put some points on the board and give it a run um towards the end. So, we didn't. Um, you know, it's a divisional game. Uh, it it really hurts to >> their come out like that. >> Their run game, I think, ended up at like 325 yards around there. Just what happened there, do you think today? >> Yeah, I think I'm not sure the stats. I got to watch the film. But, um, thought we did a good job, you know, up until the fourth quarter. I think the first um you know three quarters I really thought we contained and I think in that fourth quarter it really got out of hand. Uh but that's what happens when you know I think they attempted maybe four passes or whatever it was. Uh you got you got to bring your hard hat and and be able to stop the run and like I said we didn't do that. Um and I thought that you know their defense did a good job of stopping our run. So that's what it comes down to at the end of the day. How do you uh evaluate a game like this coming off of it? Like what can you take anything from the film because the conditions were just so strange? >> Yeah, absolutely. You can still take away there's a lot to learn from. >> Um you know, we're going to see these same runs. We're going to see these same gap schemes. Um you know, people are going to load the box. You know, they feel like that's going to be the answer to beat us. And uh we just got to be able to come in next week and be more prepared of uh stopping the run and run the ball better. >> You were very complimentary of Mike this week. How do you help him bounce back from this performance? >> Yeah. Um, you know, that dude's dealt with a lot of adversity um in his career. I don't think that this um this is a small thing to him. Uh but yeah, it it hurts. I mean, you you see him in this locker room. He's heard about it. Um he's feel like he he's let our team down, you know, in that turnover margin. Uh but yeah, I know he'll bounce back. I know I know the person uh I know the player that he is, and I know there's better days for him, for sure. You had a touchdown saving play poking the ball out from Bucky Irving there in the first. How difficult is a player like him to defend? >> Yeah, he's, you know, he's not your traditional back. Um he's almost similar to our number seven over here and um you know, you think the play's over. Uh they run these duo runs that's supposed to hit downhill and uh you got to cover every single gap with number seven. And uh like I said, I thought we did a good job of containing him um up until a couple big runs that he had. Uh much respect to those guys and uh we'll see them again though. >> How do you describe like having the momentum from beating an unbeaten team like the 49ers last week, the high of that win and then coming in here and being shut out today? >> Yeah. Um you know, it's es and flows of of you know, the NFL. Um nobody cares what you did last week. Um you know, you're going to get your best from everybody week in and week out. So, uh, there's there's still stuff to learn from like like we said last week, when you come off that type of win, there's still a lot of stuff to clean up. Um, but there's also great things that, you know, you want to continue to build on. So, uh, we we did some great some good things as well today, I think. Um, but, you know, it kind of outweighed, you know, the worst, the the bad, outweighed the good. So, uh, we just got to bounce back. >> How frustrating was it to just not get the offense in a rhythm? like felt like maybe on that final drive things were starting to click with the big reception to Dodson but just nothing really getting going until late in the game. >> Yeah, it was frustrating obviously as a offense old but sometime some weeks are just like that and we'll just do a better job of trying to make sure it doesn't happen again. >> How much did the weather conditions affect you guys? I know Kendall Daniels said not an excuse but how does it really affect the way the offense operates? I mean, it's >> it was tough. Obviously, it was just raining a lot, but it wasn't I wouldn't say affected anything different. Just change the uh style of how you had to win. >> And now the team falling to three and five, nine games left of the season. Kind of at that halfway mark. Where do you guys go from here and reset for next week? >> Just watch the film. Um get ready for Madrid next week and try and get a win next week. >> Any words to Mike after his performance today? Probably not the one he wanted to have. >> Yeah, I think he's fine. Obviously, the stats may not um marry up as how we feel, but it's we still have all the belief in him. >> Kendall, how much did the weather have an impact in this game? >> Uh, it changed the game. We knew that it was going to run the ball and we [snorts] just got to do a better job of knowing what they were going to do and we knew they weren't going to pass it and we just got to do better job. I got to do a better job um and fits and knowing that they're running the ball and just uh tightening up my chin strap and being ready to go. >> Yeah. Over 300 uh rushing yards for them. just how difficult was it to contain their run game? >> Um, a lot of the stuff was on us and just being on me, just being out of my gaps and um being able to make the plays when they were there. Um, they were slippery, so we just got to be better. Um, I got to be better getting the call in and and being able to make the play for my team. >> What makes it difficult to play against a player like a dynamic Bucky Irving? >> Um, he's a great player. You know, he's a he's a great back. He's slippery and with the rain he's even more slippery. He's a great player. He made a great a lot of great plays and uh give credit to him. >> You now fall to three and five about the halfway mark through the season with nine games left. How do you guys regroup and go on from this? >> Yeah. Um it's just a mentality. Um 1 and0 every week and we didn't go 1 and0 so we'll move on and we'll try we'll we'll go one and0 next week and just um look what we can learn from this and just keep looking forward. >> Last time a team won a game without completing a pass was 1974 if I'm not mistaken about that. when you go in and you know they're about to run the ball and you just can't slow it. How hard is it to handle that as a defense? >> Well, we just got to be um better. I got to be better mainly just being able to stop the run as the mic linebacker. Have to be able to it's me versus the running back and just be able to get him down more times than I did. Um but we just we just got to do all around better um better job just containing the run when when we know it's run. >> Was it about what you watched on tape? Was there anything new they tried today, do you think, or? >> Um, a lot of stuff was on us. Um, a lot of the stuff was just, you know, uh, I was out of my gap a couple times and they hit a couple big runs and, you know, just taking that and and put it all on me. Um, I just I have to be better. >> I know starts have been a common theme, but how would you evaluate the way the defense came out in the first half holding Tampa Bay to just three field goals? Um, yeah, we wanted to start fast and just be able to play with short fields and just being able to play. Um, we just got to be able to put our feet in the grass and play and we we started to get leaky in the second half and we have to play all four quarters on defense. Um, not have some good drives and and then let them go for big runs, but um we'll get in a lab and and figure it out and watch film together tomorrow and we'll get better from here. >> John, 16 to nothing shut out loss against a divisional opponent. just how do you describe the emotions after a game like this? >> Yeah, it was tough obviously. Um not the outcome we wanted. Um you know, they they played better than us today. Um that's really all uh tough, you know, um circumstances that we had to deal with with the the weather and everything, but uh it's no excuse. Uh we got to come out and play better. Um and luckily we they're a division opponent and we get to see them again. You said it's no excuse, but how much did the weather have an impact in today's game? >> A lot. U can't even lie to you. A lot. Um it's really hard to throw the ball downfield when it's downpouring um the entire game. Uh your socks are filled in puddles and it's just it's a lot. Um but like I said, it's no excuse. Uh we got to execute at the end of the day. Um and they did that better than us today. >> Slow starts have kind of been a common theme this season. And how frustrating is it to kind of not get things clicking until the end of the game? >> Yeah, it it's very frustrating because, you know, it's all on us. Um it's all on us to to come out there and and start fast and execute the right way. Um at the beginning of the game, from the start of the game to the end. Um so it it is frustrating uh just because it's self-inflicted. Um we got to get better. Um we got a lot of football ahead of us. Um we're going to we're going to be >> Around 100 receiving yards for you today, the most as a Falcon. How does it feel to just get more involved and contribute to this team? >> I want to win. Uh simple as that. Um this stuff doesn't doesn't mean too much to me when we don't come out on top at the end of the game. Um I want to win for this football team. I want to be a contributor into winning for this football team. Um that's all that really matters to me. >> How did Mike handle today, do you think? >> I think he handled it well. Um obviously he wants some plays back. Um we all would. Um, but you know, like I said, it was tough conditions out there. Um, and I think he he he played the best he could.

title: Instant Reaction To Bills 36-10 Win Over The Ravens | Bills Postgame Live | Buffalo Bills
text: Buffalo's offense lit it up in the second half scoring 20 points beating the Ravens 36 to 10. Welcome into Bills postgame live. He's Bills legend George Wilson. I'm Maddy Glab. Buffalo's offense came to life in the second half. Drives stayed alive. They scored touchdowns on three of five possessions compared to just one of eight in the first half. George, what was the biggest difference in the second half for Buffalo's offense? >> One, they protected the football a lot better in the second half. Much better, you know, than they did in the first. And then those penalties, you know, when you time you have penalties and turnovers, those are drive killers. And ultimately they made some adjustments at the half, came back out in the second half, sustained the drive, stayed ahead of the chains, stayed on schedule, and able to make those converted those drives into points. >> Josh Allen finishes with 289 passing yards. Speaking of sustained drives, it was good to see Allen link up with some of his receivers in the second half. That was a little bit of a struggle in the first half and catching those passes made sure that Buffalo's drives ended in touchdowns in the second half. >> Yes, coming into the game, we knew that we had to take advantage of those matchups on the outside. Coming into week eight, the Ravens versus the pass defense against their pass offense of of their opponents were giving up targets to 78% of the time to their wide receivers. So there was opportunities on the outside. DJ Moore coming back into the lineup getting a 49-yard reception. Dalton Kincaid provided several ex- a few ex-plays in the game today and that allowed that big play component to return to the Bills offense. As a result, scoring a lot more points and and holding on to that 30-plus yards points per game average. >> Dalton Kincaid leads the way for Bills receivers. Four catches, 86 yards and a touchdown for Kincaid. Awesome to see him be a big playmaker against the Ravens defense. Bills quarterback Josh Allen on the podium right now. Let's head over to QB1. >> Tomorrow we trick or treat tonight? >> Uh no. No trick or treating. We just stay at the hotel, you know. >> Would it be fair to say that wasn't despite 36 points, which is crazy, not the sharpest day for the offense? >> Yeah, the first half was in our standards really bad. We didn't play up to our standard. Um weren't throwing and catching it. Um didn't feel like I was I was doing a good enough job. Um obviously the the couple turnovers in the front in the first half it's it's not winning football. And then sitting there with talking with the guys in that second half or going into halftime just saying, "Hey, we're we're way better than this." Um let's just focusing on the details. We went out there I don't couldn't tell you our second half splits, but that second half is who we want to be. >> Josh, you had a 39.8 QB rating at halftime. You finished with over 96. You're you're huge. All right, but uh what did uh what do you what do you what do you feel that what it took to like get you guys in sync in that second half? >> Again, just sitting there talking to ourselves and saying, you know, we're we're better than this. Um trusting each other, trusting the guys on the field, trusting what the the call was. I think early on I was for whatever reason was felt like I was pressing. Um so we can't do that. Um now granted we'll we'll we'll take wins when we can get them whether it's by one or whatever the total is here. 26 that quick math. >> How do you make yourself stop pressing? >> Like when you say you were pressing and then you just weren't pressing anymore. >> Take a breath, settle down, settle the feet down, and just go through your progressions. >> Can you talk about DJ's return? Obviously some big plays there. What does it mean to have him in the back field? >> I mean it's the the the big pressure obviously the big post is unbelievable catch. Um that's the type of you know, spark that he gives us um where we don't have to go these long sustained drives. He gives us that downfield presence. Um and the run after the catch stuff. And obviously we got to clean up the ball security. He knows that, you know, I I threw an interception today, so um again, got to find find better ways to hold on to the football, but um you know, he's he's an absolute stud and the more more we can get him the ball the better our offense is going to be. >> Sorry, Josh. For the for as exceptional as the numbers have been for you guys as an offense, you've had stretches like today. Um so is there going to be a through line where you guys cuz you guys eventually have found it in almost every game. Has there been a through line where you guys go through a stretch like the first half tonight? >> I mean, the the other team gets paid, too. That's a really good defense we just played. Um there's a lot of great talent on it. So, they're going to have a game plan coming into it. Um you know, sometimes it just takes a little longer to figure out what the defense is trying to do, and I think we're we're really good at making adjustments. Um coaching staff and individuals and and players that we have. Um so again, once we feel like we kind of understand what's going on within the flow of the game, I think that's when we start playing better. Now, obviously, we want to start faster. Um that's no secret. So, again, we'll watch the film and then we're on Monday night next week. So, again, extra day to kind of digest it and continue to get better. >> How do you think this Tyler Kreigbaum handled the challenge of >> I'm so proud of him. He again, throughout the week, not sure if he was going or not. Um and just decided, "Hey, I'm going to plan like I am." Um and I thought thought he played fantastic. >> Coach, we already know how difficult it could be for offense to really get in sync coming off the bye week, but can you talk about how that defense was out there balling? >> Oh, man, our defense balled out tonight, and um again, I I said this in the the interview after. I hope their quarterbacks, especially, you know, not especially, but Lamar and and Tyler are doing okay. Um you hate to see guys go down in this game. It's an extremely violent game. text: 3 1 2 3. Hello Bills Mafia, we know there's something on your mind every day.  His team, the Buffalo Bills. title: Drake Maye on 2nd half: "We Started Playing Complimentary Football." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Trick, you said you got your arm wrapped around your shoulder at the end of the first half of the game.  What did it magically give you in the second half to get on the field?   I would like to say that it was a magic touch.  We just, you know, started to follow through on the attacks.  We made some big plays, which helped .  We had a few good receptions with the runs, which was nice.  But we really started running the ball well .  It was nice to see that.  And then we started playing coordinated team football. How did this game-changing play affect the team's momentum? Um, that touchdown, yeah, I think that was a huge moment.  We needed to open up the game a little bit and, you know, break the barrier by getting into the scoring zone.  And I think we did it.  I think the coach was a little blunt about us hurting ourselves.  You know, with Coach Vrabel and Coach McDaniels.  We hindered ourselves and stopped the attacks, but I think they did a good job at first .  I think, coach, you know, the Dolphins have a good plan.  They put a little pressure on us at the beginning, but we got used to it and found our rhythm. What was Coach Vrabel's message at halftime? He just said we wanted to start the game quickly.  We failed.  So he said to stick together, not to fall apart , it's the same message as throughout the year.  Be the decision yourself.  Don't wait for anyone else.  Go and do it yourself. I think everyone got the message, and we felt like we did it.  It was nice to see such a performance from the boys. Regardless of who is available at the wide receiver position, how important was it for Kyle and Pop to make those big plays down the field? It was huge.  Guys, you know, first of all, they always do everything right .  I think it's their credit for blocking in the takeaway game, they get the award .  And I think Pop is hard to stop.  He's hard to stop when he breaks out to the edge of the field, and you saw that during the touchdown.  So, it was good that Kyle got, you know, another, deep pass. And we need to give these guys the ball in space more often, because they know how to run . He also made a crucial play on third down. Yes, that's her.  First of all, it was a great ball reception.  He keeps proving his worth, and after that early fumble, I just told him not to stop and keep playing .  This is, in fact, the NFL.  This happens .  And, you know, we did it. What did you think of what you saw during that touchdown run?  Simply Yes, when we play this combination, you always feel a little drive.  It's, you know, like Mandre and I are two for one.  Like a quick breakaway in basketball, you hope to force your opponent to make a mistake, and we did that.  So I'd rather give the ball to Mandra.  You know, in college we did 90% passing and 10% taking out .  So I'm happy to be that 10%. How hard was it to lose Hunter and what adjustments did you have to make afterward? Yes, it's always hard to lose Gant.  You know , when Gant and Eli were on the field, we were already short of receivers.  These guys will be very important for us.  Gant and Eli adjusted well to the weather, and the infield play was not bad.  We felt like we had a chance to work inside, and that's hard.  I saw him when he got up after the reception, I was worried about him, although I probably shouldn't have been.  But I'm worried about Gant, I know he went to the locker room, but he looks fine there.  He seems to be walking and smiling normally.  So he remains himself. How would you describe the conditions, their impact on the game, and how much they tested you?   Can you feel the suit?  Carolina blue. We were convicted last night, man.  We were convicted in the game against Miami.  But, no, I think under these conditions we knew it would be difficult.  We knew it would rain the whole time.  Then we went out for a warm-up, and, um , sorry, guys.  I don't know whose it is. Sorry.  Um, we went out for a warm-up, and everything was, everything was perfect.  And we thought , you know, the ball would be a little sticky.  I thought I would have a good chance of throwing it.  And then you come out here again, and the rain is pouring down like a bucket.  And you come back at the end of the fourth quarter, and it's pouring again .  So we just fought, knowing that the ball was the most important thing.  We knew it.  And we knew they were a team that would knock the ball out .  So I tried to play reliably, without losing the ball.  We didn't get it, but I felt like once Chase...we knew ball control was going to be really important. And I thought I had a good view of the field, trying not to put the ball in danger in this weather, and I threw it to Eli, like I gave him a little push.  So I should have given him a little better pass. What was your last question?  What was key for you in staying patient with the receivers, given the conditions, not trying to force things in the first half, and how did you make sure you were effective? Yeah, I think, coach, we did a good job of calming down and figuring out what the weather would be like, considering our divisional opponent. To see, you know, the new head coach, to see what they were trying to do to us, and I was just trying to adjust.  And I think we moved forward, we moved forward, but we didn't make a field goal once.  We had a chance to keep scoring points and we knew once we calmed down and had a few drives we would have a chance to score points and I think we still lost a few chances.  So we need to get back to work. Do you think there was perhaps too much caution in the first half because of the weather, and in the second half you started running more? Yes, it matters.  You know, this ball, you see, there are different moments with the weather, it can be a problem.  And you know, the ball isn't always, um, you know, nothing personal against Jared, but the guys up front are just rolling it on the grass, and the grass is wet, and they, he doesn't really care much about football , and he shouldn't.  He has to block a 300- pound man.  So, um, sometimes these guys, EQ, you know, kudos to the EQ guys, they did a good job of keeping the balls dry, and, um, we did n't really have any issues with that, but I definitely think it affects seeing how their offense plays, how we play, and building a game from that.  And I think Coach McDaniels is one of the best at adapting to that.  It was like, you know, the Denver game, it was the same.  You know, in the playoffs you just have to look at the weather and how we play.  So, thank you guys. Thank you.

title: Zyon McCollum, Alex Anzlaone & More on W vs. ATL | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How are you feeling? >> Uh, I mean, I don't mean to toot our own horns, but we set a franchise record rushing, so feeling on top of the world right now. >> And just what does it mean to win a game and allow Baker to have a another game where he doesn't have to throw too much out there? >> Yeah, I mean, it's great. I mean, it's just a testament of our offense, the O-line. I mean, the tight ends, the wide receivers, running backs, just It's just everyone doing their job, and I mean, Baker, he's He hands off a mean ball, so really hats off to him as well. >> That's about five weeks that you guys are getting in a groove, getting your chemistry down. How good does it feel to do that? >> Yeah, I mean, it feels great. I mean, I don't like to look at statistics that much, but I mean, I'm assuming we're going to be leading the league in rushing. I think I mean, last week, I mean, the Cowboys, Thursday night football at Cowboys, I mean, just I think we run the ball well, and I mean, we got a great quarterback who can throw it as well. But yeah, it feels great. >> Look, when you when do you guys on the O-line start to kind of commit to the bit there knowing that we're not going to pass the >> I mean, I I think I can speak for all five of us. We prefer to run the ball, so we're begging for those runs. Uh, I mean, obviously, we're in the position where we can run the ball. It's not like we're chasing or anything like that, but we really like to put the guys on our shoulders and really show show showcase what we can do and everything. I mean, I'll die on the hill that we're the best O-line in the in the country, so. >> Do you have any thoughts on that? >> Uh, I mean, just got to keep stacking them. I mean, obviously, the beginning of the season, like Coach Bowles said, the first quarter of the season didn't go as we planned; but we're in the second quarter now, and, uh, I believe we're tied for first place, and I mean, just need to keep building week after week. >> Do you know you guys set a franchise record in rushing yards today? >> Yeah, I did. We did We did know that. I think the previous was 283, and now I think we're at 320, so we're all we're all pretty high on life right now. I mean, but that's the next goal, break that. But yeah, it feels great. >> How good of a locker room is Baker? I saw that you were in there with him on the sidelines screaming. >> Yeah, he was in the in the mud puddle over there. He's great blocker. He took Bates all the way to almost took him back to his locker room. Yeah, but it was like a puddle over there. I thought someone was going to drown, but Bates, yeah, he he throws some great blocks, too. I mean, um just guys get on space and he's he's run down the field and Bucky makes a guy miss and and Bates throws a block. I mean, that's just testament to the selflessness that we have on this team. >> Just what can you say about this offensive line? Obviously, you're going in there and and you heard you heard all the crap, you know, in the first quarter of the season. >> Oh, yeah, everyone heard the crap about apparently how we're horrible Excuse my Excuse my French, but a a bad O-line. Um I I I mean, I would I would argue that I can I mean, I would love to for someone to put on the tape and tell me how we're a bad O-line, pass blocking or run blocking. Grant Burton. >> a question >> Yeah, what do you got? >> After missing out on all the fun last week, are you excited to be back with the fellas this week? >> Yeah. I was disappointed. All the runs I got last week watching it at home, I like, "Dang, I would miss this game." Little would I know that we're going to run it more this week. And that that just made me so happy. [laughter] Yes, absolutely. >> Things just all the little things are starting to coming together that I talked about earlier in the season. Just finding up on those details, those similar things. We're starting to learn how each other plays. We can play off of each other a lot faster, a lot easier. And so, coverage seems seamless. >> How much pride do you guys take in pitching a shutout like this? >> Tremendous pride. I mean, the coaches are on us heavy throughout the second half. It's a 0-0 game, no matter how much points get put on the board, that's our mindset. And so, that's just what we what we how we see it. >> Zion, just what's what's been clicking for you guys? And do you notice that there is from the first quarter to now the last few games, like you guys are understanding each other more? >> 100%. I think we were finding our identity and we've been sharpening up on details and I think now we kind of understand who we are as a team. You know, we're able I know who my teammates are and so I know their strengths, their weaknesses and vice versa. And so because of that, we're able to uh play a little bit better off of each other. >> What's it like watching that offensive line and Bucky and Kenny go to work knowing I think it's the first time since 1974 the team has won a game without throwing a pass. >> Yeah, that that's wild. I mean, I was talking everybody. I was like, "In 10 years it's going to end up on NFL Films or something." Because I mean, it was just an incredible game from those guys. They're super selfless. You know, the O-line, that group, they're they're super close together and I think the entire team kind of models how close they are off of that group just because they're a family, you know what I mean? And so to see them go out there and execute, to see Bucky and and KG, you know, find the holes and get yards, that's all the motivation we need on defense. >> What was your reaction seeing Zyonne with back-to-back interceptions? >> I was stunned. I was stunned that he was able to catch it, honestly, in the rain. Like, hats off to him. You know, he's an incredible player and he's the the leader and the rock of this defense. And you know, he's constantly on us all the time and we make sure to give him some, too, but he went out and got it today. >> What were those field conditions like? What was it like playing in that monsoon earlier? >> It was terrible. I mean, I'm not going to sugarcoat it. The field was terrible in the first half. Second half, I mean, it was a little bit better, but I mean, you're kind of not really playing on grass, you're kind of playing on mud and dirt. So, but no excuses. It's like that for everybody. So, we take pride in that. We know the conditions here in Tampa. It's going to rain a lot. So. >> Two straight wins. Just how did you guys pull off this? How does this momentum in your favor, I guess? >> Yeah, I mean, we first of all, I don't celebrate like it's the Super Bowl, you know? We just won two games in a row. We still have a lot of season left in us. And so, just continue to stay on the details, continue to keep doing the things that are working, and Sunday night football's coming. >> And you win a game where the guy doesn't have to complete a pass. >> Yeah, it's exciting. 300 and what? 20 yards on the ground? Yeah, we'll take that. >> Just What does it mean as an offensive line to dominate like >> Yeah, it's pretty cool. Um It's a nice feeling like >> There you go, Sam. >> You know, we knew we were running it, they knew we were running it. Um I mean, it really got set up by the defense. I mean, kept giving us turnovers, giving us giving us good field position. We even got a couple field goals off it. So, imagine, you know, if we can capitalize off those. Same thing kind of in Carolina last week. Got us good field position off of off of interceptions and turnovers and, you know, we ended with field goals, but we want to end with end with touchdowns and, you know, we're even happier, but um Yeah, it's fun. Three three three I don't know what the exact one was. 320-something on the ground. Um Franchise record. In the peanut butter. In the peanut butter. Um yeah, it's pretty sick. >> What is that like for you guys? Like you said, they know you're running and you're running it, but you're still imposing your will and you're getting it done. What does that say about this team? >> I think we're just a gritty outfit. You know, it was a gritty football game. Um Yeah, I mean, I love the guys in here. Um you know, I think Danny Smith said it best, you know, we kept saying everyone's like, you know, we got to dig ourselves out, got to dig ourselves out. And Danny Smith said, "Just quit digging." I was like, "Damn." I was like, "That's a pretty good quote." Um so, yeah. It's just a testament to the guys in this room. and we we we we never wavered. We kept, you know, continuing to put in the work, continuing to grind, continuing to come in every day with a good attitude and and and and getting better. Yeah. >> How much enjoyment do you guys get out of a sloppy rain-filled mud bowl and, like you said, just imposing your will? >> Yeah, I love it. That was so much fun. I just think that's uh and the epitome of what this team is this year, just gritty, grimy, just some I don't know. Stick your nose in there and and and get after it. Um but no, it was a lot of fun. It was a lot of fun today. >> On the building. >> What was that like for you? >> It was cool. Um you know, the second one is kind of like, "Damn, he's really throwing the ball to me again." So, yeah, it's hot in here. It's hot in here. So, um yeah, it's it's the first one, you know, you just you react to the play. >> It was a quick, quick, uh, slant backside, and I was able to make him. And then, the the, the second one was a, you know, a dig coming front side to me. And, um, you know, just when you get in those moments, it kind of feels like slow motion. Just luckily, I was able to catch the ball. >> Four turnovers last week and four this week. What's working for you guys on defense? >> Uh we're just attacking the ball in the air honestly. You know guys are making great plays when the ball's in the air and you know JP had that one and then the screen and go that Zion caught was really impressive too. So guys are just playing with good vision on the quarterback and you know matching the routes properly and you know we're getting the ball when when the ball goes in the air. >> What was it like playing in those conditions? >> Uh it was fun honestly. As a linebacker you like to play in those. You know they're going to run the ball and we got to stop the run and you know we knew coach Bowles kind of you know set set our mindset going into the the week once we found out it was going to be this type of weather. You know it's going to be a seven stud game with our cleats and you know all weather gloves and or no gloves and you know stop the run. >> And also just what was it like watching the offense do their thing and the fact that you guys were able to win a game without completing a pass? >> Yeah I mean that's pretty crazy. That's probably some historical stat but okay. Yeah it's a long time and football's changed a lot since then too. So, you know, it's impressive. And you know, we played into the weather, and you know, when we get going, it seems like, you know, it's hard to get us off track. And you know, it's just a lot of guys straining in the run game offensively to, you know, strain on their blocks and, you know, get those extra yards and, you know, couple break away runs. >> A little bit of a rough start to the season but you guys are two and oh in the NFC South right now. Just what does it say about you guys sticking together, sticking to your process, and not listening to the outside noise? >> Yeah we're stoic. We're stoic. Coach Bowles sets a good you know tone for the team and you guys know he's a very stoic guy. He doesn't get too high too low and when the winning happens it's you know the same level of uh stoicism that you know a lot of the guys in this locker room have. We a lot of guys have won in this locker room and they know what how to treat it and how to go about their business. So we just got to keep stacking them and and stick to the process. >> What's the difference between the first quarter of the season to the second quarter? >> I think the biggest thing is just us being able to close out games, us being able to finish. That's been the biggest thing. >> And then also, what is it like to watch the offense do their thing and to know that you can win a ball game without Baker completing a pass? >> It's been special just to see them be able to go out there and play smashmouth football. Just to just be able to go out there and play grown man football been I've been really impressive to watch from the sideline. >> What can you say about Jacob Harris and what he's been able to do here this second year? >> Um going to be special. I think he's having a tremendous year. Same with Zion. I think they're both playing at a extremely high level. So, we're going to need them to continue to keep keep playing at the level that they're playing at and and we feed off them, everybody going to keep keep going. And um as far as like Keionte, we need him to keep coming too cuz he's been making some plays. And we just need him to continue to make plays down the stretch as we try to go on this run. >> Thank you. What is it like playing in the rain so much ball? Like it sounds like it takes you back to being a kid, right? >> Yeah, definitely takes you back to being a kid. But uh you know what type game it is, you know what's going to happen. It's going to you're going to have to impose your will. They're going to try to line up and run the ball. You got to be able to strike blocks, get off blocks. You can't go one for one and be able to tackle the ball carrier. >> Have you ever been a part of a game, probably not in your professional career, but even when you were a little kid where no passes were completed and you still won? >> No. No. Um I think 2022 year at Georgia, I don't know if we threw the ball much against We played Kentucky. It was like really cold and the winds was crazy. So, both teams just ran the ball and we won like 16-6 or something like that, but that's that's the as the closest game I can remember. >> And then two straight wins, just how does that help this team out here? >> Uh it's it's big. I think we got to continue to build off that, continue to build off that momentum. And especially, I think any divisional win is an important one. >> Another interception for you today. Was to make two this year, four in your career. Just what was the secondary? What was going well for you guys today? >> Shoot, I just think we do a good job communicating back there. And I think all year we've been doing a good job making plays on the balls. Uh that's what we get paid to do. I think we're doing a good job doing that. >> What's been the biggest difference between the first quarter of the season and the second quarter right now in the >> I mean, I feel like it's been the same. Uh every game we come with that mentality. Uh just just to bring it every single game. You know what I mean? I think we're a defensive team. That's what coach Bowles says, so knowing the game will fall in our hands. So, we got to have that mindset every single time we uh step on the field. >> How much pride is there in going out there and and pitching a shutout? >> Uh a lot of pride. Uh that's a hard thing to do in the NFL and uh I'm very proud of the boys we did that, but it's on to the next week. >> What does it mean to watch the offense do their thing and know that you can win a game without them completing a pass in the process? >> It means a lot. Uh that run game is is very important in the NFL. It's It's important in it later in the season when it gets cold. So, us being able to run the ball right now, but we got to carry on that later when we're trying to get to the playoffs. >> What was it like playing in that weather? >> Uh it's fun, to be honest. Like playing little league football, that's all I think about. Uh Well, I mean I I feel like we at least going to have them one of those games every single year, so I take pride in I mean, I'm two for two anytime it rains at home, so I like it a lot, to be honest. >> And just what does it mean to get another win in the division? I know that I mean, despite the start, you guys are only a half game out of that NFC South lead. >> I mean, yeah. It's very important uh if we win all our division games, we we go to the playoffs. That's what coach Bowles says, so we take pride in each division game, but uh it's on to the next week. We got a big game next week and looking for that opportunity.

title: Steelers LOVE rookie S Robert Spears-Jennings, Keeanu Benton breakout, DL growth | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all the Pittsburgh Steelers uh practice today. From an injury standpoint, it's pretty clean overall. They have their guys on IR, but Tevin Slater and Brandon Echols will not play. That will cause a shift in the uh special teams unit. Terrell Edmunds will come up um and play. I believe we'll see some Sean Davis and Bunchy Stallings. You might even see a little bit of Daelin Hayes on special teams, but no Brandon Echols or Tevin Slater. I do think they will get Ben Snell back, which will be a nice boost, but I think Brandon Smith will still play some special teams for them. Um and and Alex Highsmith, who was limited the last 2 days with a groin issue, should play. He played through it last week, should play through it again this week. I thought the biggest story today was talking to secondary coach Teryl Austin Jr. about Robert Spillane and he took us through essentially the whole process of how they found him. When they talked to him through the process, they thought he was smart. They thought he was disciplined. They thought he had great studying habits. And they thought the only reason he fell was because of his processing and eye discipline. Uh he said that he had dirty eyes in college. When you watch the Oklahoma tape, he allowed a lot of explosive plays, but this kid was explosive. He was extremely fast. He played physical and he had the right mentality to him. And and you're basically betting on pedigree there, right? You're drafting him because of the pedigree. He said the only reason he fell to the seventh round was because of his eye discipline. That's the only reason. And safeties are guys that naturally fall. If you don't have a pretty pretty perfect profile, you're probably not going to go very early as a safety. Robert Spillane has done such a great has done such a great job. And so even with Devin Bush and Vince Williams back, expect this kid to continue play. This team loves Robert Spillane. They love what he brings to the table and he is such a diligent worker that takes the criticism and doesn't take it personally. That's great. Karl Dunbar, Steelers defensive line coach, also talked today just about some things. One, he's showing the team his highlight tape from the time he played with the Bengals, the Broncos, a few other teams in there. This guy was a nose tackle in the NFL for 15 years and he was relentless and he was strong. He's a big man that played with great pad level. And he said he's seen it in Gabe Rivera Rubio and Isaiah Buggs. Taking that, Isaiah Buggs' pad for example has improved dramatically over this year compared to last year's tape. But even Keanu Benton, you know, he's the light has gone for Keanu Benton. They looked at his quickness, his explosiveness. He was a typical 4-3 technique. And that's what he's been for a lot of this year. They've run some of 4-3 looks, they've run some different looks, and he's been playing a three-tech or four-eye a lot. Lot less nose tackle. Why? Because of his quickness and explosiveness. And Keanu Benton seeing double teams over 50% of the time. But it's translated as chaos making not only from the pass rush game, but into the run game. And that's made him significantly much better. And and and we talked to Keanu today, and Keanu said, "Listen, it just feels like it's slower. I'm seeing the field better. I'm seeing what's going on a lot more." And so I think that is is a big thing for them. The Steelers will obviously face the Browns on Sunday. First place in the AFC North up for grabs.
